stance_basis: letter supports ORV use and EO 11644 implementation but objects to draft's negative tone, weak secretarial review guidelines, and lack of scientific criteria for bureau heads
summary: Ed Youngblood, Associate Director of the American Motorcycle Association, submitted a formal comment letter supporting the general goals of Executive Order 11644 and the Department of the Interior's ORV management efforts, while raising several specific objections to the draft environmental statement. He argued the draft was negatively toned and discriminatory toward ORV users, that bureau-level implementation without stronger secretarial oversight and scientific guidelines was contrary to the spirit of the Executive Order, and that terms like 'irretrievable and irreversible damage' were unsubstantiated. He also offered constructive suggestions including adopting AMA noise standards and collaborating on scientific land-use guidelines.
complaint_summary: Youngblood's letter argues that the draft EIS is negatively toned and discriminatory toward ORV users, that placing total implementation responsibility on bureau heads without secretarial-level scientific criteria is contrary to the spirit of Executive Order 11644, that terms like 'irretrievable and irreversible' are unsubstantiated given the acknowledged data gap, and that noise standards and a collaborative scientific land-classification effort should be pursued.

statement.text:
I have had an opportunity to examine the environmental statement draft dated May 26, 1972, and I would like to congratulate your bureau and the Department of the Interior for its continued diligent efforts to administer the public lands under its jurisdiction. Reflected first in the task force study on off-road recreational vehicles that began in 1971, these efforts attest to the positive direction and purpose that appears again in this most recent statement.
Please be assured once again that the American Motorcycle Association is at your service in the implementation of guidelines for land use brought about by Executive Order 11644. As motorcycling's only national organization, representing the more than 4,000,000 motorcyclists of the United States and having an active membership of 150,000 individuals, we feel that we have the desire and facilities to serve you in achieving policies for land use which will be fair to all concerned.
In a climate of constructive dialogue, please allow me to comment on the environmental statement draft of May 25th at this time.
First, as you point out in the draft, there certainly are alternatives less desirable than the proposed implementation which will include secretarial review. It would be contrary to the spirit of Executive Order 11644 to entrust implementation of the order to the bureau level without secretarial review. Such action would be contrary to the recognition of off-road vehicle use as a national issue, which is, in fact, one of the ramifications of the order. Also, the full closure of public lands is out of the question -- as the draft states -- and contrary to the goals and responsibilities of the Department of the Interior.
However, we would like to suggest that the proposed guidelines for secretarial review are weaker than they might be. For example, respective bureau heads may determine the vehicle usage in the National Park Systems, Natural Areas, Natural Wildlife Refuges and Game Ranges. These include vast areas, and it would seem that the

June 21, 1972 page 2
placement of total responsibility on the respective bureau head is tantamount to localizing implementation of Executive Order 11644, which is contrary to the spirit of that order. There must be some type of scientific criteria established by the Department of the Interior which would influence and aid the respective bureau heads in implementation of the order.
Basically, throughout the draft, the tone is negative and discriminatory toward off-road vehicle users. There is continual restatement of the position that trails may be established only if the bureau head determines that off-road vehicle use will not adversely affect the natural, aesthetic or scenic values. The draft fails to emphasize the responsibility of the bureau head to indeed determine these facts. To the contrary, he may comply with the standards established in the draft simply by making no determination whatsoever, stating that adverse effects are likely in his judgement.
Again, I believe this possibility indicates the need for a definite set of scientific guidelines for the individual bureau heads to follow.
Your department, of course, is aware of this need, since it was expressed early in the Task Force Study on Off-Road Recreational Vehicles. On page 68 of that study is the paragraph, "The Task Force believes that essentially what is necessary to plan adequately for outdoor recreation and ORRV use is a land classification system specifically designed to protect the resources, provide safe and sane recreation and allow for as rational and balanced, yet diversified, an outdoor recreation program as possible providing a place for the motorized vehicle user on public lands within this framework should be possible without lowering other outdoor recreation standards."
This statement by the Task Force reflects very accurately the feeling of the American Motorcycle Association, and of the AMA-Motorcycle Industry Council Combined Committee on Land Use. This committee, composed of delegates from the AMA and the MIC, presently is reviewing resumes by professional ecologists. The group has resolved to hire one of these gentlemen for the purpose of establishing guidelines in a very comprehensive and clear textbook fashion. Through such a set of guidelines we hope to establish fair and equitable use of the land, knowing full well that some public land will be lost to the use of off-road recreational vehicles, yet with the feeling that our effort to cooperate will be returned by those with other interests.
Since the AMA and the MIC already have begun work towards such a set of guidelines, perhaps the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation or the Department of the Interior would be interested in working with us on such a study. I am sure that you will agree that such a study is necessary for proper implementation of Executive Order 11644.

June 21, 1972 page 3
We would submit that certain words and phrases appearing in the draft should be eliminated altogether in order to establish a fair and objective climate for implementation of Executive Order 11644. For example, on pages 12 and 15 appear references to substantial irreversible and irretrievable damage that can be caused by off-road vehicles. However, on page 13, significantly falling directly beyween these two statements, is the statement, "Data regarding these concerns is less than satisfactory. Individual bureaus (coordinated by the Assistant Secretary - program policy) will monitor the effects of off-road vehicle use on land under their jurisdiction to close this information gap." As the draft rightly points out, there is indeed an information gap and a lack of satisfactory data, so it would follow that in addition to being very negative in tone, the words "irretrievable and irreversible" are factually incorrect at this time, and, in fact, may not be justified at all by subsequent study. We feel that the appearance of such unsubstantiated words and statements in the draft reflects a prejudice against off-road recreation vehicles which is indeed an opinion rather than honest fact, and it would appear that this attitude is somewhat less than fair in regard to the 5,000,000 families presently using off-road recreational vehicles.
In regard to muffler and silencer specifications, we would suggest that this area be strengthened from the position it currently takes in the draft. Not only should mufflers be required as the draft states, but they should be required to meet standards. Please let me suggest that on motorcycles they might be required to meet the standards which have been established and enforced by the American Motorcycle Association for two years. The AMA currently sanctions 7,000 events annually and over 6,000 of these events are run according to an AMA standard for mufflers and silencers which requires each machine to emit a sound no greater than 92 decibels, measured at a distance of 50 feet. We have found this standard to be very workable and satisfactory, to be very instrumental in reducing the level of offensive noise, and at this time it has been enforced and practiced for a substantial period. We would suggest that it might be an expedient standard to be adopted by the Department of the Interior as well.
In closing, please let me comment of the general theme of the draft which seems to be an effort to assure that the public will not be harrassed by motorcyclists and off-road recreational vehicle users. In accordance with the original Executive Order 11644 and with the Department of the Interior Task Force Study, please let us suggest that it is also the obligation of the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation to minimize conflict among users, and not to single out one particular group as the cause of conflict. Following this philosophy, we hope that your bureau will take as much care to assure that motorcyclists and off-road recreational vehicle users are not harrassed as well. If the Federal Government truly recognizes

June 21, 1972 page 4 5
the number and legitimacy of motorcyclists as suggested in Executive Order 11644, it would seem to me to be the legitimate and logical task of the Department of the Interior and its separate bureaus to provide for these people. In short, contrary to the tone of the Task Force Study and the Executive Order 11644 which seem to propose the accommodation of off-road recreational vehicles, the environmental statement draft presents a somewhat more negative approach, with a good deal less emphasis upon the needs to diligently pursue a scientific and organized program of land classification leading to fair land use.
I hope these comments have been helpful. Please do not fail to contact the American Motorcycle Association if additional information and dialogue is needed. We are at your service, and have a sincere desire to help with implementation of the Order.
Sincerely
Ed Youngblood
Associate Director
